analysis:
Examined both inference.md excerpts and the supplied change map/patch against the indexed threat model and full T-041 definition. The visible substantive change at head lines 810–813 documents accepting variable-frame-rate GLM video and sampling by frame index divided by nominalFrameRate; head line 829 removes its former deterministic rejection. This expands admitted media inputs at TB-007, but the surrounding patch retains decoded-frame and prepared-pixel caps, media reservations, exclusion from prefix reuse and target-only decoding. Documentation alone does not establish a bypass or availability regression.
Head lines 205–248 describe scoped resident prefix caching and retained memory charges; these are outside the complete changed ranges, so their tension with T-041's SSD-only production posture is not attributable to this PR. Likewise, the supplied base Flint/Bonsai/tool-validation material does not establish a changed control. No supplied change alters encryption, authorization, attestation, billing or secret exposure.
Integration must verify the changed GLM runtime's VFR sampling and bounds: nominalFrameRate validation, sampling arithmetic, decoded-work limits, cancellation and reservation lifetime for adversarial videos. The corresponding implementation is not supplied here. The added head lines 876–880 are also absent from the text excerpts and truncated patch; their security implications remain unexamined. These PR-specific coverage limits require deeper review, rather than an unsupported finding.
